title: Training Albatross  An Expert Finance LLM: Leo Pekelis
talk_summary: Leo Pekelis of Gradient describes building a finance-domain LLM via automated data curation (membership-inference filtering of already-seen data, human review, synthetic augmentation), continued pre-training plus SFT/preference alignment, and a 1M-token context extension to reduce hallucinations via in-context learning.

takeaways.technique: Prefer long-context in-context grounding over RAG for interrelated chunks
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue RAG fails when retrieved chunks must reference each other, and that putting more raw material directly in the prompt is the most sample-efficient way to reduce hallucination; they extend context to ~1M tokens so thousands of examples fit.
takeaways.evidence_quote: rag does typically does a pretty poort job at that ... context length is the bottleneck

takeaways.technique: Filter training/eval data the model has already seen (membership inference)
takeaways.what_they_do: They use membership-inference techniques to estimate whether a document was already in the base model's training data, discard seen data, and human-review the small remainder before synthetic augmentation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we use techniques to to try to see if a particular document uh if there's a high chance that it was already in the models training data

takeaways.technique: Few-shot with many examples when accuracy demands it
takeaways.what_they_do: They note that for many tasks thousands of in-prompt examples are needed to reach production-grade accuracy, and long context makes that feasible at inference time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: for a lot of Tas out there this like thousands of examples Mark is actually necessary uh to get kind of production grade accuracy
